title: Dynam3D: Dynamic Layered 3D Tokens Empower VLM for Vision-and-Language Navi

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Text says Dynam3D achieves modest improvements of approximately 1-2% in navigation success rate (SR) over g3D-LF and Uni-NaVid. Table 1 shows R2R-CE Val SR: g3D-LF 47.2, Uni-NaVid 47.0, Dynam3D 52.9, i.e. +5.7 and +5.9 percentage points; Test SR is 46.3 vs 51.4, i.e. +5.1. The stated margin is inconsistent with the table.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1, paragraph on REVERIE-CE and NavRAG-CE results
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Text says Dynam3D outperforms NaVid by approximately 3-5% in Success Rate (SR) on REVERIE-CE and NavRAG-CE. Table 2 shows NaVid SR 26.6 vs Dynam3D 40.1 on REVERIE-CE, a +13.5 point difference, and NaVid 19.4 vs Dynam3D 24.7 on NavRAG-CE, a +5.3 point difference. The numerical claim is not supported.

Text says removing the rendered panoramic patch tokens is row 1, but in Table 6 row 1 has both Single View and Rendered Pano set to ×, so it contains no patch tokens at all. The condition that keeps single-view patches while removing rendered panoramas is row 2, which is the comparison later used for Value of Rendered Panoramic Views. The row reference is inconsistent with the table.

Text states the impact order is Patch > Instance > Zone tokens. In R2R-CE the patch drop is larger than the instance drop, but in REVERIE-CE removing Instance causes a larger drop than removing rendered patch tokens: row 4 vs full gives 26.8 vs 40.1, a 13.3 point drop, while row 2 vs full gives 28.4 vs 40.1, an 11.7 point drop. The stated ordering is not consistently supported.

Text says: In addition to these, we perform ablation by degrading the quality of 3D instance and zone embeddings through feature dropout and spatial jitter, and claims Table 7 shows it degrades significantly more when 3D representation quality is compromised. Table 7 only reports SLAM noise and depth noise; there are no feature-dropout or spatial-jitter rows or results anywhere.

References [35] and [57] are duplicate citations of the same AAAI 2025 paper by Chen et al., listed with slightly different titles: Affordance-oriented planning... vs Affordances-oriented planning... One entry should be removed and citations reconciled.

predicted_errors.error_location: Eq. (1) and Section 3.1, Updating the Patch Feature Points
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Eq. (1) gives M_t = M_{t-1} ∪ {new feature points} as the update rule, but the surrounding method says Frustum Culling is applied first to discard outdated points and then new points are added. The update equation omits the culling/removal operation and thus does not match the described dynamic update.

The abstract claims pre-exploration and lifelong memory experiments demonstrate the potential applicability of the method, but Section 4.2 states that without stricter evaluation protocols the reported substantial performance increases may be inflated due to environment memorization or data leakage, and that controls are needed. The claim is stronger than the evidence admitted in the paper.
